newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- quiet, back to unchanged. [CORRECTED 19:02 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- quiet, back to unchanged. [CORRECTED 19:02 GMT]

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds returned to Tuesday's levels at midday Wednesday, after showing slight losses in early trading.
The more positive tone mimicked the Treasury market, which also turned positive at midday.

The government long bond was up 8/32 at 99 to yield 6.70 percent, ahead of the 1400 EDT release of the Federal Reserve's Beige Book. Analysts expect the report to provide more evidence of a second quarter economic slowdown.
Muni traders said secondary activity was light, with attention focused on a large slate of new issue pricings.

On the competitive side, J.P. Morgan Securities (corrects from Smith Barney) said it won $47 million Albuquerque, N.M., water and sewer bonds at a true interest cost of 4.774 percent. The firm reoffered 2008 bonds at 4.90 percent, and did not formally reoffer the 2009 maturity.
A total of $496 million of competitive offerings are expected Wednesday, with a $200 million Massachuesetts Bay Transportation Authority deal at 1300 EDT topping the list.

Negotiated offerings total $605 million in 14 sales. The largest was a $133 million Michigan Municipal Bond Authority deal through Bear Stearns & Co. The bonds were tentatively priced at a top yield of 5.48 percent in 2020.

Debt futures also reversed early losses at midday. September municipal futures were up 3/32 to 118-3/32, while September Treasury futures rose 2/32 to 111-30/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 197 ticks from 196 at the close on Tuesday.
In secondary trading, bids on Chicago Board of Education AMBAC 5-3/4s of 2027 were down 1/8 at 100-7/8. Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were up 1/8 to 101-1/4.
